The climate in the northern Illinois area, in which this project is located, can be characterized by cold winter months and warm summer months. It can be reasonably assumed that many of the residential buildings in the area of this proposed improvement will be air-conditioned and have storm windows several months out of the year by 1990. (See the United States Department of Commerce, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, Environmental Data Service publication "Local Climatological Data, Annual Summary with Comparative Data, Chicago, Illinois" 1972, available from the National Climatic Center, Federal Building, Asheville, N.C., 28801, Attn: Publications. The sale price is 15 cents per copy.)
Under the assumption that many of the residential structures involved with this project have or will have storm windows and central air-conditioning systems by 1950, eighteen (18) of the twenty-eight (28) residential structures for which 1990 L10 noise level predictions were made would be less than or equal to the design year interior L10 noise level standard of 55 dBA contained in PPM 90-2. Ten (10) of these structures or approximately 36% would require added noise abatement measures such as masonry reconstruction, structural framing, or window casement renovation to accommodate double glazed windows in order to meet the interior noise level standard contained in PPM 90-2.
It is recognized that the proposed improvement of Lincoln Highway between Cicero Avenue and Chicago Road will have a design year (1990) noise impact.
For the buildings subject to Land Use Category "C" of PPM 90-2, thirty-seven (37) of the forty-nine (49) buildings, for which existing L10 noise levels were measured were less than or equal to the PPM 90-2 noise level standard of 75dBA. The L10 noise levels predicted for the forty-nine (49) buildings in this Land Use Category yielded forty-six (46) buildings with 1990 L10 noise levels in the over 75 dBA range.
